name: Sources - ASA
title: NDIA Agency and Scheme Applications Policy - Mandatory Regulatory Framework Coverage
preamble: NDIA Agency and Scheme Applications Policy - Mandatory Regulatory Framework Coverage
rows: National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 and NDIS legislative instruments
Scheme applications are the digital means by which statutory NDIS functions are performed. Policy controls must keep application design and operation aligned to the Act.
Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013, PGPA Rule and NDIA Accountable Authority Instructions
Agency applications control high-value Scheme payments, obligations, evidence and service delivery; governance must be embedded in application lifecycle controls.
Commonwealth Fraud and Corruption Control Framework 2024, Fraud and Corruption Rule and Policy
Scheme and corporate applications are key controls for preventing invalid access, false claims, payment diversion and insider misuse.
Privacy Act 1988, Australian Privacy Principles and Notifiable Data Breaches scheme
NDIA applications handle sensitive disability, health, identity, financial and contact information at scale.
The policy must require application-level privacy governance that supports the NDIA privacy management plan.
Some corporate or payment-related applications may handle TFN information; it is subject to special legal protections.
Freedom of Information Act 1982 and OAIC FOI guidance
Application records, logs, decision documents, reports and correspondence can be FOI documents.
Archives Act 1983 and National Archives information management standards
Application data and records are Commonwealth records when made or received for NDIA business.
Electronic Transactions Act 1999 and Electronic Transactions Regulations 2020
NDIA applications support online forms, notices, consents, records and signatures that may replace paper processes.
Disability Discrimination Act 1992 and Australian Government digital accessibility requirements
NDIA applications must be accessible to people with disability, including participants and representatives.
Administrative Review Tribunal Act 2024, ADJR Act and administrative law guidance
Scheme decisions must be capable of review with complete evidence and reasons.
Protective Security Policy Framework 2025 and Commonwealth Technology Management Direction 004-2025
Agency and Scheme applications hold official information and require protective security governance.
ASD Information Security Manual and Essential Eight Maturity Model
Agency and Scheme applications need formal cyber controls across design, build, operation and decommissioning.
Hosting Certification Framework and Cloud Computing Policy/Standard
Scheme applications depend on hosting environments that must meet government security and sovereignty expectations.
Australian Government Digital Experience Policy and Standard
NDIS participants, providers and staff rely on digital services to access and deliver Scheme outcomes.
Digital and ICT Investment Oversight Framework, contestability and assurance requirements
Major application investments must align with government investment, assurance and reporting controls.
Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022 and DATA Scheme Code
Application data may be considered for sharing, analytics or research; the Act imposes safeguards where used.
Digital ID Act 2024 and Digital ID Rules
NDIA applications may rely on identity proofing and authentication for participants, representatives, providers and staff.
Policy for the responsible use of AI in government and AI transparency requirements
Applications may include AI, machine learning, rules, decision support or generative AI features that affect Scheme operations.
Commonwealth Procurement Rules, Digital Sourcing Framework and NDIA procurement posture
Application software, hosting, SaaS, SI, support and managed services are typically procured and must be governed.
